evidence.imagegen_prompt:
Create a warm hand-painted digital gouache 3:2 review board. Title exactly “17 · EASTERN SCREECH-OWL · Megascops asio”. Labels exactly “ADULT MALE”, “ADULT FEMALE”, “JUVENILE”. Exactly three owls.

Place the adult male at left and adult female at center on the same branch and baseline. Both are northern gray-morph Eastern Screech-Owls, never using red morph as a sex difference. The female is only subtly fuller/heavier in body volume, not taller. Both adults have a small compact body, prominent small pointed ear tufts, bright yellow eyes, olive-greenish cere and bill with yellow tip, gray-brown upperparts with black shaft streaks and fine vermiculation, a visible white scapular shoulder line, barred flight feathers and tail, whitish underparts with branching longitudinal dark lines and faint cross-bars, and tarsi feathered to the toe base. Distal toes are gray-brown and grip the branch naturally.

At right show one approximately 27–30-day brancher beside a natural tree cavity and adjacent branch. It is a fluffy gray mesoptile juvenile with very fine alternating light/dark barring across head, mantle and underparts, reduced soft ear tufts, subdued yellowish eyes, formed but incomplete wings with short soft remiges, and a short tail largely concealed by fluff. The juvenile is fully supported by wood, climbing with both talons while one short wing flutters for balance. It is not airborne.

Wooded stream or mature park habitat; warm restrained ochre and forest-green background; clear review-board spacing; accurate owl feet and support. No neonatal white ball, no mature adult wing or long tail on the juvenile, no confident flight, no spread-flight pose, no red-morph female, no size-exaggerated female, no extra birds, no hatchling, no labels other than the exact title and three exact role labels.
